A proportion of patients referred for PET imaging may require general anaesthesia or deep sedation (circa 5 per cent of patients). Although it is preferred that prospective healthcare facilities can provide this, it is not a mandatory requirement. CHI intends to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement with up to three Service Providers. However, CHI reserves the right to appoint fewer than three providers, including a single provider, where this is considered appropriate following completion of the procurement process. Services will be drawn down on a patient-specific basis. The selection of the Service Provider for an individual referral will be determined by CHI having regard to the clinical requirements of the patient, service availability and capacity, accessibility of the proposed facility, and where appropriate, patient and family preferences. CHI considers ease of access for patients and families to be an important aspect of service delivery and will take account of facility location and accessibility when evaluating tenders and making referral decisions under the framework.

title: Norway – Refuse disposal and treatment – Sanitation services for industrial waste.
description: Background The tender contest applies for the following municipalities: Harstad municipality Kvæfjord municipality Tjeldsund municipality Lødingen municipality The municipalities shall enter into a new contract for the collection and treatment of commercial waste. The municipalities have several locations with different types of activity and waste flow. This sets requirements for a system that provides better control, more enjoyable practice and simple operation across addresses and devices. There is also a need for safe systematic handling of hazardous waste and other waste fractions that require special follow-up. The aim of the procurement is to establish a uniform and operational friendly system for the collection, transport and treatment of business waste. The system shall contribute to better compliance with regulations, a higher degree of sorting, more predictable logistics and better documentation of waste management in the municipality. Description of the assignment The assignment includes collection, transportation and treatment of business waste from several locations and different addresses in the municipalities. The procurement shall cover the municipalities ́ continuous need for waste management through a combined and uniform service. The delivery shall include handling mixed commercial waste and relevant waste fractions, including food waste, glass and metal, cardboard, plastic, residue waste, hazardous waste, EE-waste, confidential waste and infected waste. The assignment also includes the necessary handling and follow-up of fractions that require special documentation and traceability. A flexible collection scheme is requested that safeguards both planned emptying and the need for extra emptying and urgent orders.
